name: Return II Space
editorial_article:
'Return II Space' is a landmark collection by Digital Mystikz, the seminal dubstep production duo consisting of Mala and Coki. Released in 2010 on their own iconic label, DMZ, the project functions as a curated anthology of tracks that helped define the 'DMZ sound'—a stark, ominous, and profoundly bass-heavy style that eschewed the commercial trends beginning to overtake the genre at the time. The album is composed of six tracks originally released as a series of 12-inch vinyl records (DMZ 015, 016, and 017), grounding the project in the sound system culture that birthed the movement in South London.

Sonically, 'Return II Space' is characterized by its minimalism, repetitive structures, and deep, sub-bass-led atmosphere. Tracks like 'Unexpected' and the title track, 'Return II Space,' embody the eerie, mechanical precision that made Digital Mystikz masters of the dubstep craft. With its focus on atmosphere over complex melody, the project evokes a sense of vast, urban isolation that was hallmark to the early sound of the DMZ dances at the Mass club in Brixton. By stripping back the sonic landscape to its barest, most effective elements, Mala and Coki created a document that remains influential for its dedication to purity, weight, and the physical impact of low-frequency sound. Mastering for the record was handled by Jason Goz, and the distinctive visual identity of the release is credited to the artist &a&k&t, underscoring the collaborative and DIY ethos that sustained the DMZ label's profound influence on electronic music.

editorial_pitch: An essential document of the 2010 dubstep underground, 'Return II Space' captures the deep, skeletal, and meditative sound pioneered by Digital Mystikz. Featuring tracks released across the legendary DMZ label, it remains a definitive exploration of the genre's space-conscious, bass-heavy aesthetic.
